keywords: Edwin Hubble and the Shattered Boundaries of the Milky Way
Discovery of Extragalactic Galaxies and the Expansion of the Universe (Hubble's Law)
full_text:
In 1929 CE, the frontiers of human understanding were transformed through the indomitable persistence of Edwin Hubble & Milton Humason.

At the time, the reigning scientific establishment in the field of Extragalactic Astronomy & Cosmology was constrained by orthodox paradigms that could no longer account for emerging experimental anomalies. While many researchers looked past these discrepancies or dismissed them as instrument artifacts, Edwin Hubble & Milton Humason recognized that the anomaly was itself a beacon pointing toward an undiscovered law of nature.

Working from primary documentation recorded in *A Relation between Distance and Radial Velocity among Extra-Galactic Nebulae (PNAS, 1929)* (Vol. 15, pp. 168–173; Mount Wilson Observatory (100-inch Hooker Telescope)), the breakthrough emerged through painstaking methodology. Every alternative hypothesis was systematically tested, isolated, and eliminated under rigorous controls.

At Mount Wilson Observatory, Hubble identified Leavitt's Cepheids in the Andromeda nebula, proving it was a separate 'island universe' millions of light-years away. Correlating distance with redshift, he proved that galaxies are speeding away from each other—the universe itself is expanding.

The discovery of Discovery of Extragalactic Galaxies and the Expansion of the Universe (Hubble's Law) did not merely answer a localized puzzle; it triggered a profound paradigm shift across Extragalactic Astronomy & Cosmology. Today, its principles form the bedrock of modern empirical science, reminding every student that progress is forged when courageous curiosity meets disciplined observation.
